content: If you are interested in taking over this page and applying to become the Editor-in-Chief for this topic, you are welcome to do so. There can be one or more Editors-in-Chief for this topic. Additionally, you may apply to serve as an Associate Editor-in-Chief for one of the subtopics listed below. To express your interest in either role, please send us an email. Be sure to include your CV and/or a biographical sketch as part of your application. Overview: Pungency refers to a sharp and biting sensory impression. In the context of chili peppers, it is scientifically equivalent to the Scoville scale, which measures the spiciness or heat level of these peppers. Mechanism: The sensation of pungency caused by compounds such as capsaicin, piperine, and allicin is mediated through the activation of the TRPC1 ion channel. This channel, which is sensitive to heat and acidity, is located on nociceptors, the nerve cells responsible for sensing pain.
